newsitem.title: UK: LME markets mixed at close, trade slow throughout.
newsitem.headline: LME markets mixed at close, trade slow throughout.

text.p: Base metal activity remained slow during Monday afternoon LME trading, with markets trapped in unexciting ranges, traders said.

Copper business was confined to an extremely tight $11 band, with the market showing little enthusiasm for tackling the $2,500 level overhead. The spread backwardation did widen slightly, which maintained a steady undertone.
"It is a sideways market, and that is what is keeping the lid on movements and volumes," one said.

By the end of the kerb three months prices were at $2,488, up just $1 a tonne from last Friday's kerb close. In the short-term, jobber activity will predominate between $2,475 and $2,500, traders say.

Aluminium displayed a steadier sheen after some early forward buying flipped the market above $1,600, although the upmove ran into a buffer of resistance around $1,690. Last trade was at $1,603, up $6.
Nickel's performance was lacklustre and after aimlessly ranging around $7,300 for most of the session prices tailed away during the kerb.
The market closed at $7,250, down $60, and continue to wait for developments at the strike-bound Inco Sudbury facility.
Zinc lost ground during the day, staging a mini-correction to Friday's advances to fresh 4-1/2 year highs, and final trade was $11 easier at $1,356.
The tin market was less heated on the spread front, as the contango reverted back to around $45/45 after touching $14 last Friday.
This defused a rally in forward values, with three months closing at $5,580, down $130.
Lead was confined to a $4 band, and closed at $641, down just $1. Alloy ended at a stable $1,472/75.
